(not provided) #### **3.1.3.1. Floating-point Registers** There are 32 FRs, denoted as `f0` - `f31` , each of which can be read and written. Only when only floating-point instructions that manipulate single-precision floating-point numbers and word integers are implemented, the length of FR is 32 bits. Under normal circumstances, the length of FR is 64 bits, regardless of the LA32 or LA64. There is an “orthogonal” relationship between basic floating-point instructions and floating-point registers, that is, from an architectural perspective, any floating-point register operand in these instructions can use any one of the 32 FRs. .
